History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
19-year-old female university student with 6-day history of dysuria, urinary frequency, and mild suprapubic ache with pink urine today—clinical picture most consistent with an uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).

History:
• Presenting complaint: Burning/stinging on micturition, increased urinary frequency, and mild lower abdominal (“bottom of tummy”) ache.  
• Onset/duration/progression: Began just under one week ago; symptoms persistent without significant change.  
• Hematuria: First noted pink-tinged urine today; no frank red blood reported.  
• Suprapubic pain: Dull, aching; worse during urination; does not radiate to back or flanks.  
• Associated symptoms: Denies fever, chills, rigors, nausea, vomiting, flank pain, or new bowel changes.  
• Bowel history: Known IBS with variable stool form and frequency; no new symptoms.  
• Gynecologic/sexual history: Combined oral contraceptive pill; long-term boyfriend; last unprotected intercourse 1–2 weeks ago; last menstrual period 2 weeks ago; no abnormal vaginal discharge.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None specified.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No headaches, chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, or systemic symptoms.

Past Medical History:
• Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS); takes antispasmodic (see Medications).  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Combined oral contraceptive pill – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Mebeverine (patient unsure of exact name; antispasmodic for IBS) – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• Clindamycin – adverse reaction unspecified.

Social History:
• Lives in university halls with flatmate; first-year English student.  
• Tobacco: Does not smoke; tried cannabis once 1½ weeks ago.  
• Alcohol: Drinks socially.  
• No regular illicit drug use reported.

Family History:
• No known bladder, kidney, or other relevant hereditary conditions.

Physical Examination:
• No in-person examination performed during teleconsultation; no vitals recorded.

Investigations:
• Planned: Mid-stream urine for dipstick, microscopy, culture, and sensitivities.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis)
  • Plan:
    – Empirical oral antibiotic: Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin 3-day course (choice to be finalised after urine result).  
    – Submit urine sample today for MCS; adjust antibiotics per sensitivities.  
    – Hydration: Encourage increased oral fluids.  
    – Analgesia: Paracetamol as needed.  
    – Safety-net: Seek urgent care if develops fever, flank/back pain, vomiting, or worsening hematuria.  
    – Follow-up: Re-assess if no improvement in one week or sooner if symptoms escalate.

General plan items
  • Discussed recreational drug use; advised avoidance for health reasons.  
  • Reinforced contraception adherence and pregnancy considerations if symptoms persist.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but expected: Vital signs, physical exam findings, full drug list with dosages, detailed allergy reaction description.  
• Internal conflicts: Symptom duration described as “few days/3 days” then clarified to “just under a week” (conflict noted).  
• Transcript quality: Good audio with minimal omissions; no significant inaudible sections.
